label: Fed Funds Rate
value: 3.50–3.75%; September 15-16 Hike Odds ~58% After Waller's Dovish Signal Was Reversed by a Blowout August Jobs Report
source: Federal Reserve FOMC, July 29 2026 (held); Waller Speech, Sept 3 2026; BLS Employment Situation, Aug 2026 (released Sept 4); CME FedWatch, Sept 4 2026
delta: Waller's Sept 3 dovish remarks briefly cut hike odds to ~48-55%; the Sept 4 jobs blowout (+162K vs +53K expected) reversed that, pushing odds back to ~58%
deltaNote: SEPT 3 UPDATE: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech that if incoming data continued to show disinflation over the next two weeks, he would 'be inclined to support holding' rates at the Sept 15-16 meeting — a notably more dovish read than Chair Warsh's hawkish Aug 28 Jackson Hole keynote. CME FedWatch hike odds fell roughly 9-18 points (estimates ranged ~48.4%-54.6%) from the prior day's ~66%. SEPT 4 UPDATE: The August jobs report reversed the dovish move within 24 hours — nonfarm payrolls surged 162,000 (vs ~53,000-56,000 expected), unemployment held at 4.1%, and June/July were both revised up a combined 55,000. CME FedWatch hike odds jumped back to ~58% (up ~9 points on the day); the 10-year Treasury yield rose nearly 3bps to 4.79%, back near its Sept 2 cycle high of 4.814%. Compounding the hawkish inflation risk, renewed US-Iran strikes across the Gulf (Sept 1-6 — Kuwait, UAE, and mutual Strait of Hormuz tanker strikes) kept Brent crude on track for an ~8% weekly gain, reinforcing the 'higher-for-longer' case into the Sept 16-17 FOMC. Prior: Aug 28 Jackson Hole keynote turned hawkish, pushing hike odds to ~57% from ~35%; July 28-29 FOMC held at 3.50-3.75% with 3 hawkish dissents.

label: US 10Y / 30Y Treasury Yield
value: 10Y at 4.79% (Sept 4) — Retested the Sept 2 Cycle High of 4.814% (Highest Since Nov 2023) on the August Jobs Blowout
source: CNBC / Federal Reserve H.15 / FRED / Yahoo Finance; July 23 - September 4, 2026
delta: Waller's Sept 3 dovish remarks pulled yields down briefly, but the Sept 4 jobs blowout reversed the move — the 10Y rose nearly 3bps to 4.79%, back near its Sept 2 high, while renewed Gulf strikes (Sept 1-6) kept an oil-driven inflation premium under the long end.
deltaNote: SEPT 2-4 ARC: The 10Y touched 4.814% intraday Sept 2 (highest since Nov 2023) as a synchronized global bond rout — Japan's 10Y above 3% for the first time since 1996, Germany's Bund at 3.375% (highest since 2011), UK gilts at 5.25% (highest since 2008) — combined with renewed Strait of Hormuz tanker strikes. Fed Governor Waller's Sept 3 remarks, signaling openness to a September hold if disinflation continued, pulled yields off that high. The move reversed within a day: BLS's Aug jobs report (Sept 4, released same day) showed nonfarm payrolls +162,000 (vs ~53-56K expected) and June/July revised up a combined 55,000 — sending the 10Y back up nearly 3bps to 4.79%, within striking distance of the Sept 2 cycle high, as CME FedWatch hike odds jumped to ~58%. The 30-year's Aug 17 peak of 5.31-5.32% (highest since June 2007) remains the cycle high. National debt concerns (nearing $40T), stubborn above-target inflation, and a still-unresolved US-Iran Gulf conflict (renewed strikes Sept 1-6 across Kuwait, UAE, and the Strait of Hormuz) remain the structural floor under long-end yields heading into the Sept 16-17 FOMC.

label: Michigan Consumer Sentiment (August 2026 Final)
delta: +0.7 vs preliminary (51.0); still -6.3% vs July final (55.2)
deltaNote: AUG 2026 FINAL (released Aug 28): 51.7, revised up from the 51.0 preliminary but still down 6.3% from July's final 55.2 and roughly 11% below a year ago. Current Economic Conditions fell 5.3% to 51.9; Consumer Expectations fell 7.0% to 51.5. One-year inflation expectations eased to 4.0% (from 4.2% preliminary); long-run expectations held at 3.3% for a third straight month. Sentiment fell across all political groups, sharpest among Republicans, older consumers, and lower/middle-income households. Still well above May 2026's all-time record low of 44.8, but the reading — alongside July retail sales' steepest drop in over a year — underscores the crack in the 'resilient consumer' narrative that Warsh's same-day hawkish Jackson Hole keynote did nothing to ease.

label: S&P 500 / Market Risk Gauge
value: S&P 500 Holds Within ~1% of Record Highs (7,718.60, Sept 4) Despite the Jobs-Driven Yield Spike and an Unresolved Gulf Conflict
source: AP / Yahoo Finance / CNBC / The Motley Fool / Federal Reserve; July 23 – September 5, 2026
delta: SEPT 3-5: Stocks rallied Sept 3 on Waller's dovish signal (S&P +1.1%, Dow +1.2%, Nasdaq +1.4%), then slipped Sept 4 (Dow -0.51% to 53,414.25, S&P -0.38% to 7,718.60, Nasdaq -0.29%) as the blowout jobs report revived hike bets; the VIX remained low (~14.5) into the weekend even as the US-Iran Gulf conflict escalated further.
deltaNote: AUG 27-SEPT 4 ARC: The market's Aug 27 record run gave way to a hawkish Jackson Hole keynote, an Aug 31 Mideast strike, and a two-day Sept 1-2 slide/rebound around a global bond rout. Sept 3 brought a broad rally (S&P 500 +1.1% to ~7,750, Dow +1.2% to ~53,685, Nasdaq +1.4% to ~26,584 — the best day in weeks) after Fed Governor Waller signaled openness to a September hold, even as Iran launched a second night of retaliatory strikes on Kuwait and the UAE. That reversed Sept 4: the blowout August jobs report (+162,000 vs ~53-56K expected) sent the Dow down 271.86 points (-0.51%) to 53,414.25, the S&P 500 down 0.38% to 7,718.60, and the Nasdaq down 0.29% to 26,506.99, with CME hike odds back to ~58%. Despite the whipsaw, the S&P 500 remained within about 1% of its all-time high and the VIX stayed low (~14.5), even as the Gulf conflict widened further over the weekend (US tanker strikes and Iranian reprisals, Sept 5-6) — a striking calm relative to the stacked macro and geopolitical risks.

label: US Avg Effective Tariff Rate

source: USTR / Global Trade Alert / Bloomberg / AP; July 24 - August 25, 2026
contestNote: US-Canada trade talks collapsed late Aug 21; the Section 338 tariffs (50% on ~$20B of Canadian autos, alcohol, and dairy) took effect Aug 22 (after a brief 3-day suspension from the original Aug 19 date). Carney declared Canada 'at war' with the US on trade. On Aug 25, Carney announced Canada's countermeasures: tiered 15%/25%/50% retaliatory tariffs on ~$20B of US goods across 700+ products (steel, aluminum, furniture, clothing at 50%; appliances, dairy, seafood at 25%; other industrial goods at 15%), effective September 8, plus a C$7.5B (US$5.4B) support package for affected workers and businesses. Two days later (Aug 24) Trump additionally threatened 50% tariffs on Canadian autos, auto parts, and steel starting Jan 1, 2027. Separately, the Section 122/Section 301 transition (60 economies, 10-12.5%) that resolved July 24 remains in force; USMCA-qualifying goods stay exempt from Section 301.

label: Global Policy Uncertainty / Recession Risk
value: SEPT 6: Gulf War Escalates Further (Tanker Strikes, Naval Blockade Clashes) as a Blowout Jobs Report Reverses a One-Day Dovish Fed Signal
source: Federal Reserve / BLS / ADP / ISM / China NBS / Census Bureau / U. Michigan; July 17 – September 6, 2026
delta: SEPT 3-6 ARC: Fed Governor Waller's dovish Sept 3 signal was reversed within a day by a blowout August jobs report (Sept 4), while the US-Iran Gulf conflict widened into a multi-country exchange (Kuwait, UAE, mutual Hormuz tanker strikes) with no sign of de-escalation into the weekend — reinforcing both the inflation-hawk case for the Fed and the oil-supply-shock risk to growth.
deltaNote: SEPT 6 RECESSION RISK SNAPSHOT: Two risk channels are now moving in the same direction. (1) LABOR/FED: Waller's Sept 3 remarks briefly cut September hike odds to ~48-55%, but the Sept 4 BLS report (nonfarm payrolls +162,000 vs ~53-56K expected, unemployment steady at 4.1%, June/July revised up 55,000 combined) reversed that to ~58%, with the 10Y Treasury back near its Sept 2 cycle high (4.79% vs 4.814%). (2) GULF CONFLICT: The Sept 1 US strikes near the Strait of Hormuz triggered a widening Iranian response — retaliatory strikes on US-linked bases in Jordan, Kuwait, and the UAE (Sept 2-3), then a direct IRGC ballistic-missile attack on a US carrier group answered by the US destroying three Iranian tankers, with Iran hitting six more vessels in reprisal (Sept 5), and further IRGC attacks on US warships claimed Sept 6 alongside a harsher Iranian rhetorical line ('the era of proportionate responses is over'). Brent crude is on track for roughly an 8% weekly gain. Despite the stacked risks, US equities remain within ~1% of record highs and the VIX stayed low (~14.5) — a resilience that could unwind quickly if the Gulf conflict or the Sept 16-17 FOMC surprises to the hawkish side. Also in play: Canada's retaliatory tariffs take effect Sept 8, and China's slowdown remains unresolved. Next catalysts: Canada tariff effective date (Sept 8) and the September 16-17 FOMC meeting.

label: BOJ Policy Rate
source: Bank of Japan, June 16 2026 (25bp hike — highest since 1995)
deltaNote: June 16: BOJ hiked 25bp to 1.00%, the highest level since 1995, in a 7-1 vote (Asada dissenting) — citing Iran-war energy-cost pass-through risk. The hike landed the same day Warsh's first FOMC opened, raising August-2024-style carry-unwind concerns; the immediate market reaction was orderly (Nikkei +0.46%), but the yen still fell to a fresh 40-year low past 162/USD by June 30 despite the hike and an estimated $72.5bn in prior FX intervention.
